knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Backend dtype dispatch mismatch for unsupported tensor dtypes
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend implementations may not support the same dtype/operation combinations as CPU, and unsupported dtype/backend pairs can surface as opaque dispatch-time runtime errors instead of clear validation failures.

risk_dimensions.shape: 2D matrix inputs with varied shapes, including small, large, square, and rectangular dimensions
risk_dimensions.dtype: Boolean dtype and other non-default dtype combinations
risk_dimensions.device: Backend-specific devices such as MPS; device placement constraints for both operands

failure_mechanism.description: Backend dispatch may lack proper dtype support validation for certain operations, causing unsupported dtype/backend combinations to fail with opaque function-state runtime errors rather than clear unsupported dtype messages.

input_exploration: Generate tensors with boolean and other non-default dtypes on backend devices to probe dispatch coverage
Vary 2D matrix shapes, including degenerate, square, and rectangular dimensions
Test the same operation across multiple backends to identify dtype support mismatches
constraint_awareness: Backend dtype coverage may be narrower than CPU coverage
Boolean tensors may be unsupported or may behave differently for linear algebra operations
Both operands must satisfy backend and dtype dispatch constraints
oracle_strategy: Monitor for opaque function-state RuntimeError signals
Compare behavior and results against CPU or another backend where the dtype is supported

transferability.reason: This knowledge applies broadly to APIs where backend kernels may have narrower dtype coverage than CPU. It highlights the need to probe dtype/backend compatibility for tensor operations beyond the original API.

important_considerations: Probe dtype support across available backends for common tensor operations
Check backend dispatch behavior for unsupported dtype/device combinations
Include boolean and other non-default dtypes in backend-specific fuzzing
generation_strategy: Create fuzzing harnesses that iterate over dtype and backend combinations for tensor operations, emphasizing non-standard dtypes such as bool. Treat opaque backend dispatch errors as signals and compare behavior against reference backends to detect coverage gaps.
